title: Designing for Failure and Controlled Degradation
objective: Name timeout, retry, and user-visible degradation for at least three dependencies, and record a retry budget that cannot exceed a stated NFR.
whyThisMatters: A design that only describes the happy path is a hope. Timeouts, retries, and what the user sees when a dependency is down are architecture, not afterthoughts — they decide whether a partial outage stays partial or becomes a self-inflicted cascade.
evidence: A failure-mode table covering at least three dependencies, each with a named failure, a timeout in milliseconds or seconds, and the user-visible degradation
An ADR stating the retry budget (maximum attempts and backoff) and the NFR that budget is not allowed to exceed
A note marking at least one dependency as non-retryable, with a reason that is not 'it is simpler not to retry'
acceptanceCriteria: At least three dependencies each have a named failure mode, a timeout number, and a user-visible degradation that is not 'show an error page' for every row.
The ADR states a retry budget as maximum attempts plus backoff, and names the NFR (latency, availability, or a retry-amplification ceiling) that budget must not exceed.
At least one dependency is marked non-retryable with a reason tied to a side effect, an idempotency gap, or a cascade risk — not to convenience.
